what_was_missed: The hospital discharge summary of 24 May 2023 explicitly required post-discharge blood tests every 5–7 days because of acute kidney injury; no blood test was taken at any point between discharge and readmission 36 days later, and the home could produce no system or policy for ensuring discharge summaries are actioned.

coroner_concerns.quote: On discharge to Cann House the discharge summary from Hospital made it clear that because of her acute kidney injury she should have post discharge monitoring blood tests every 5-7 days. This was not done and it was accepted by the home that this meant no one was monitoring Pam 's bloods from the day she left hospital until she was readmitted to Hospital by on 29th June 2023

Cann House missed an opportunity to carry out regular blood tests on Miss George between 23rd May and 29th June. These blood tests may have identified the need to continue to treat acute kidney injury which if left untreated may have affected her resilience to infection. The system for ensuring that discharge summaries are actioned was not available for me to see and I was not clear if any policy on this issue existed.

I am not satisfied that the breast infection was adequately managed at Cann House it being noted that there was no record of how the breast infection was progressing between 25th May and 27th June 2023

inclusion.adjudication_note:
The clearest cross-organisational instance in the corpus so far, and materially different from the hospital-internal cases. Here the information that would have changed the outcome was not merely present in a record — it was an explicit, actionable, time-bound instruction written into a discharge summary, and it simply evaporated at the boundary between hospital and care home. Thirty-six days of no monitoring. Note the compounding pattern on 27 June: the home documented 'Red raw' breasts and a fall on the same day a clinician attended and was told about neither. Two independent information channels — the discharge instruction and the day-of observations — both failed to reach the person who could have acted.

Category is 'Care Home Health related deaths', not the hospital category the harvester crawls. This matters for coverage: the discharge-boundary cases, which are arguably the most relevant to WardSafe's thesis, are systematically filed outside the category being screened. See VERIFICATION-LOG coverage note.
